question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spines.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A typical flower has four main whorls — Calyx (sepals), Corolla (petals), Androecium (stamens, the male reproductive part) and Gynoecium (carpels, the female reproductive part). (पुष्प के भाग — बाह्यदलपुंज, दलपुंज, पुमंग, जायांग)

 

• Spines are hard, pointed, modified structures found on stems or leaves (as in cacti and roses) that serve mainly for protection against herbivores and to reduce water loss — they are not one of the floral whorls.

 

• Since a flower's structure is defined by its four whorls, Spines are not counted among them, making it the odd one out among the options.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Androecium is the male reproductive whorl made up of stamens, each consisting of a filament and anther.

 

• Gynoecium, though not listed as an option here, is the innermost whorl comprising the carpel(s), stigma, style and ovary.

 

NOTE

 

• Androecium (Option 1): It is the male reproductive organ of the flower, made up of stamens.

 

• Corolla (Option 2): It is the whorl of petals, usually the most colourful part of the flower, attracting pollinators.

 

• Calyx (Option 4): It is the outermost whorl made up of sepals, which protect the flower bud.

question: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Benaras.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Benares Sanskrit College, also referred to as the Hindu College, Benaras, was established in 1791 at Benaras (Varanasi) by the British Resident Jonathan Duncan, with the aim of preserving Sanskrit learning and Hindu law and philosophy. (हिंदू कॉलेज, बनारस — 1791)

 

• It was one of the earliest institutions of higher learning set up by the British in India, and it later evolved into the Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.

 

• This is distinct from the more famous Hindu College, Calcutta, which was founded much later, in 1817, by David Hare, Raja Ram Mohan Roy and others.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was founded much later, in 1916, by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, and is a separate institution from the 1791 Sanskrit College.

 

NOTE

 

• Mathura (Option 1): No college of this name was established here in 1791; Mathura is better known for its association with Lord Krishna and ancient Kushan-era art.

 

• Kolkata (Option 2): The (unrelated) Hindu College, Calcutta was founded here, but only in 1817, well after 1791.

 

• Patna (Option 4): No 1791 Hindu College was established in Patna.

question: Where is the Gulf of Mannar located?
option_1: Between the south-eastern tip of India and the eastern coast of Sri Lanka
option_2: Between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka
option_3: Between the south-eastern tip of India and the north-western coast of Sri Lanka
option_4: Between the south-eastern tip of India and the southern coast of Sri Lanka
solution_text:
The correct answer is Between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gulf of Mannar is a large, shallow bay of the Indian Ocean lying between the south-eastern tip of Tamil Nadu, India, and the western coast of Sri Lanka. (मन्नार की खाड़ी — भारत-श्रीलंका के बीच)

 

• It is connected to Palk Bay further north by a chain of low islands and reefs known as Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu).

 

• The Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, India's first marine biosphere reserve, lies within this gulf and is renowned for its coral reefs, seagrass beds and rich marine biodiversity, including dugongs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve was established in 1989 and stretches from Rameswaram to Kanyakumari along the Tamil Nadu coast.

 

• The Palk Strait, lying to the north of the Gulf of Mannar, separates the Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu from the north-western coast of Sri Lanka.

 

NOTE

 

• Eastern coast of Sri Lanka (Option 1): The gulf lies opposite Sri Lanka's western, not eastern, coast.

 

• North-western coast of Sri Lanka (Option 3): This description more closely matches the Palk Strait/Palk Bay area, not the Gulf of Mannar.

 

• Southern coast of Sri Lanka (Option 4): The Gulf of Mannar does not extend along Sri Lanka's southern coast.

question: Who among the following won a Gold Medal at the 2021 World Cadet Wrestling Championship held in Budapest, Hungary?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Priya Malik.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Priya Malik, a wrestler from Haryana, won the gold medal in the women's 73 kg freestyle category at the 2021 World Cadet Wrestling Championship held in Budapest, Hungary. (प्रिया मलिक — विश्व कैडेट कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• She defeated her final-round opponent to clinch the gold, emerging as one of India's promising young wrestling talents.

 

• The UWW (United World Wrestling) Cadet World Championships feature wrestlers up to the age of 17, serving as a stepping stone for future senior-level competitors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Geeta Phogat, Vinesh Phogat and Pooja Dhanda are senior Indian wrestlers who achieved success at the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and World Championships, but they were not part of the 2021 World Cadet Championship.

 

NOTE

 

• Geeta Phogat (Option 1): India's first female wrestler to win a Commonwealth Games gold (2010), but not connected to this event.

 

• Vinesh Phogat (Option 2): A multiple-time Commonwealth and Asian Games medallist wrestler, not part of the 2021 Cadet Championship.

 

• Pooja Dhanda (Option 3): A World Championship bronze medallist (2018) in the senior category, unrelated to this cadet event.

question: Sangeet Kala Acharya Award is given by which organisation every year since 1993?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madras Music Academy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Kala Acharya Award has been conferred every year since 1993 by the Madras Music Academy, Chennai, to honour eminent Carnatic musicians and dancers for their lifetime contribution to the arts. (संगीत कला आचार्य पुरस्कार — मद्रास म्यूजिक अकादमी)

 

• The Music Academy, Madras, was established in 1928 and is one of the most prestigious institutions promoting Carnatic music and Bharatanatyam in India.

 

• The Academy's most prestigious title is the Sangita Kalanidhi, awarded annually since 1929 to a distinguished musician who also delivers the customary Presidential address at the academy's December music season.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Academy's annual December Music Season in Chennai is one of the world's largest cultural festivals of classical music and dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta School of Music (Option 2): A Kolkata-based institution focused mainly on Western classical music training, unrelated to this award.

 

• Shankar Mahadevan Academy (Option 3): An online music-learning platform founded by musician Shankar Mahadevan, not associated with this award.

 

• Subramaniam Academy of Performing Arts (Option 4): Founded by violinist L. Subramaniam, it promotes music education but does not confer the Sangeet Kala Acharya Award.

question: Which of the following is an example of a non-tax revenue source for the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fees and fines.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Non-tax revenue refers to government income from sources other than taxes, such as fees, fines and penalties, dividends and profits from public sector undertakings, interest receipts, and grants. (गैर-कर राजस्व — शुल्क और जुर्माना)

 

• Fees are charges for specific services rendered by the government (e.g., passport fee, court fee), while fines and penalties are levied for violation of laws — both are non-tax sources since they are not compulsory levies on income, property or transactions.

 

• Non-tax revenue also includes receipts from currency and mint, external grants, and surplus profits of the RBI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tax revenue in India is broadly divided into direct taxes (income tax, corporate tax) and indirect taxes (GST, customs duty, excise duty).

 

• Dividends from public sector enterprises and the Reserve Bank of India's surplus transfer are major components of the Union government's non-tax revenue.

 

NOTE

 

• Personal income tax (Option 2): This is a direct tax levied on individual income, a tax-revenue source.

 

• Corporate income tax (Option 3): This is a direct tax levied on companies' profits, also a tax-revenue source.

 

• Value-added tax (Option 4): VAT was an indirect tax on the sale of goods (now largely subsumed under GST), and hence a tax-revenue source.

question: Sangeet Natak Akademy Awardee Sulochana Chavan was a famous ________ singer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lavani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sulochana Chavan, popularly known as the "Lavani Samragni" (Queen of Lavani), was a renowned Lavani singer from Maharashtra, honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. (सुलोचना चव्हाण — लावणी गायिका)

 

• Lavani is a traditional folk music and dance form of Maharashtra, characterised by powerful rhythm and often performed to the beat of the dholki.

 

• She was also conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 for her contribution to Lavani music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lavani songs are traditionally performed by women dancers wearing nine-yard sarees, accompanied by dholki beats, and often address social and romantic themes.

 

NOTE

 

• Giddha (Option 1): A folk dance form of Punjab, traditionally performed by women.

 

• Jhumair (Option 2): A folk dance-cum-music form popular among tribal communities of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.

 

• Ghumar (Option 3): A traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, performed mainly by women during festivals.

question: Which of the following plants is used to cure cold and cough?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tulsi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum / Holy Basil) is a widely used medicinal plant in Ayurveda, valued for its properties in treating cold, cough, fever and respiratory disorders. (तुलसी — सर्दी-खांसी में उपयोगी)

 

• Tulsi leaves contain compounds with anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial and expectorant properties that help relieve congestion and soothe the throat.

 

• Tulsi is also considered a sacred plant in Hindu households and is commonly used to prepare herbal teas ('kadha') for immunity, especially during seasonal changes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other plants with medicinal uses include Neem (skin ailments, antibacterial) and Ashwagandha (used as an adaptogen/stress reliever).

 

NOTE

 

• Babool (Option 2): *Acacia nilotica*, mainly used for its gum, bark (in tanning) and as fodder/fuelwood, not primarily for cold and cough.

 

• Jamun (Option 3): *Syzygium cumini*, its fruit and seeds are traditionally used to help manage diabetes, not cold and cough.

 

• Arjun (Option 4): *Terminalia arjuna*, its bark is traditionally used for heart (cardiac) ailments, not cold and cough.

question: Which is the colloquial term to describe the occurrence of pre-monsoon rains in India especially in parts of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mango showers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mango showers is the colloquial term for the pre-monsoon showers that occur in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu during the summer months (April-May), which help in the early ripening of mangoes. (आम की बौछारें — केरल, कर्नाटक, तमिलनाडु)

 

• These localised, pre-monsoon thunderstorm showers occur due to local convection and moisture influx ahead of the onset of the south-west monsoon.

 

• They are of great agricultural importance as they help ripen mango crops and prepare the soil for the coming monsoon season.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The onset of the south-west monsoon over Kerala typically occurs around 1 June each year.

 

NOTE

 

• Kalbaisakhi (Option 2): Pre-monsoon thunderstorms that occur in West Bengal, Assam, Bihar and Odisha, also called 'Nor'westers'.

 

• Nor Westers (Option 3): Another name for Kalbaisakhi — violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms of eastern and north-eastern India, not Kerala/Karnataka/Tamil Nadu.

 

• Orange showers (Option 4): Not a recognised meteorological term for Indian pre-monsoon rainfall; it is a distractor option.

question: The name ‘Piyadassi’ is associated with whom among the following Mauryan kings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashoka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Piyadassi' (meaning "of pleasant appearance" or "gracious of mien"), along with 'Devanampiya' ("beloved of the gods"), are epithets used for the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in his edicts and inscriptions. (प्रियदस्सी — सम्राट अशोक)

 

• Ashoka's own name is rarely mentioned in most of his edicts; he is instead referred to by these titles, and his personal name is confirmed mainly through the Maski and Gujarra edicts, which explicitly mention "Ashoka" alongside these epithets.

 

• Ashoka, the third Mauryan emperor, ruled from around 268 BCE to 232 BCE and is renowned for adopting and propagating Buddhism after the Kalinga War.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ashoka's rock and pillar edicts, written mostly in Prakrit using the Brahmi script (and Kharosthi/Greek/Aramaic in the north-west), are major sources for reconstructing Mauryan history.

 

NOTE

 

• Bindusara (Option 1): Ashoka's father and the second Mauryan emperor, known by the Greek title 'Amitrochates'.

 

• Brihadratha (Option 2): The last Mauryan ruler, overthrown by his commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Shunga, founder of the Shunga dynasty.

 

• Chandragupta Maurya (Option 4): Founder of the Mauryan Empire and Ashoka's grandfather.

question: The festival of ‘Rath Yatra’ of Puri in Odisha is dedicated to which deity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Jagannath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival) of Puri, Odisha, is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, a form of Lord Vishnu/Krishna, along with his siblings Balabhadra and Subhadra. (रथ यात्रा, पुरी — भगवान जगन्नाथ)

 

• During the festival, the deities are taken out in three massive, elaborately decorated wooden chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple, about 3 km away.

 

• The festival is celebrated annually on Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya (the second day of the bright fortnight of the Hindu month of Ashadha, usually June-July).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jagannath Temple at Puri is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites of Hinduism, along with Badrinath, Dwarka and Rameswaram.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Ganesha (Option 2): Associated with festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi, not the Puri Rath Yatra.

 

• Lord Shiva (Option 3): Not the presiding deity of the Puri Rath Yatra; Shiva is central to festivals like Mahashivratri.

 

• Lord Hanuman (Option 4): Not connected with the Puri Rath Yatra tradition.

question: How many members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art and social service. (राज्यसभा में मनोनीत सदस्य — 12)

 

• The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) can have a maximum strength of 250 members — up to 238 representing States and Union Territories, and 12 nominated by the President.

 

• This provision allows eminent persons without a political constituency to contribute their expertise to the legislative process.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike the Rajya Sabha, the Lok Sabha does not currently have any nominated members — the provision for nominating 2 Anglo-Indian members under Article 331 was abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019.

 

NOTE

 

• 10, 20 and 15 (Options 2, 3 and 4): None of these numbers matches the constitutionally prescribed count of nominated members to the Rajya Sabha, which is fixed at 12.

question: Which of the following is NOT the socio-economic objective of Industrial Policy Statement 1980?
option_2: Consumer protection against high prices and bad quality
option_4: Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Statement, 1980 aimed at higher employment generation, correcting regional imbalances, promoting consumer protection against high prices and poor quality, encouraging export-oriented industries, and strengthening the public sector, rather than liberalising foreign investment. (औद्योगिक नीति 1980 — अधिकतम विदेशी निवेश शामिल नहीं)

 

• The 1980 policy continued India's inward-looking, protectionist economic approach, reposing faith in the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act and the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) to regulate large industry and foreign capital, rather than actively courting FDI.

 

• It was only with the New Industrial Policy of 1991 that India substantially liberalised norms for foreign direct investment as part of broader economic reforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1980 Industrial Policy also emphasised reviving sick industrial units and promoting the growth of small-scale and cottage industries in backward regions.

 

NOTE

 

• Higher employment generation (Option 1): This was explicitly among the stated socio-economic objectives of the 1980 policy.

 

• Consumer protection against high prices and bad quality (Option 2): This too was a stated objective, aimed at improving the standard of living of consumers.

 

• Promotion of export-oriented industries (Option 3): This was also an explicit objective, to strengthen India's export competitiveness.

question: In which of the following years will India host the World Badminton Championship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2026.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India will host the BWF World Badminton Championships 2026 in New Delhi, marking the return of the tournament to India after 17 years (it was last held in India — Hyderabad — in 2009). (विश्व बैडमिंटन चैंपियनशिप 2026 — नई दिल्ली)

 

• The championship is organised by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) and is one of the sport's most prestigious individual events, alongside the Olympics.

 

• India previously hosted the tournament in 2009 at Hyderabad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has also hosted major badminton team events, such as the Thomas & Uber Cup, and continues to grow as a hub for the sport following the successes of players like P. V. Sindhu, Saina Nehwal, and Lakshya Sen.

 

NOTE

 

• 2025, 2028 and 2027 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these years is when India hosts the BWF World Championships; the confirmed host year for India is 2026.

question: Grignard reagent is represented as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is CH3-Mg-Cl.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Grignard reagent has the general formula R-Mg-X, where R is an alkyl or aryl group and X is a halogen (Cl, Br, or I); CH3-Mg-Cl (methylmagnesium chloride) is a valid example of such a reagent. (ग्रिगनार्ड अभिकर्मक — R-Mg-X)

 

• Grignard reagents are prepared by reacting an alkyl/aryl halide with magnesium metal in dry ether, and are widely used in organic synthesis to form new carbon-carbon bonds.

 

• They are highly reactive organometallic compounds and must be handled under anhydrous conditions since they react violently with water and other protic solvents.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Grignard reagents were discovered by French chemist Victor Grignard, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1912 for this work.

 

• They are commonly used to synthesise alcohols by reacting with aldehydes, ketones, esters, or carbon dioxide.

 

NOTE

 

• CH3-Ca-F (Option 1): Grignard reagents are specifically magnesium-based organometallics, not calcium-based; this formula is not a valid Grignard reagent.

 

• CH3-Be-F (Option 2): This represents a beryllium compound, not the magnesium-based Grignard reagent.

 

• H-Mg-H (Option 4): This lacks the required carbon-containing (alkyl/aryl) group bonded to magnesium; it is not a Grignard reagent.

question: Which of the following crops is NOT grown during the Zaid season in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Zaid is the short cropping season between the Rabi and Kharif seasons (roughly March to June), during which crops requiring warm, dry weather and irrigation are grown, such as watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, and vegetables. (जायद फसल — तरबूज, खरबूजा, ककड़ी)

 

• Rice is primarily a Kharif crop, sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon (June-July) and harvested around September-October, as it requires abundant water and a long growing period unsuited to the short Zaid season.

 

• Zaid crops are grown mainly through irrigation on residual soil moisture, in the gap between the two main cropping seasons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's three main cropping seasons are Kharif (June-October), Rabi (October-March), and Zaid (March-June).

 

NOTE

 

• Cucumber, Watermelon and Muskmelon (Options 2, 3 and 4): All three are classic Zaid season crops, grown in the summer months using irrigation.

question: Who was the player of the match in the semi-final of the T20 Women's World Cup 2023 played between India and Australia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashleigh Gardner.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ashleigh Gardner was named Player of the Match in the first semi-final of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2023, played between Australia and India at Newlands, Cape Town, on 23 February 2023. (एशले गार्डनर — टी20 महिला विश्व कप 2023 सेमीफाइनल)

 

• Gardner's all-round performance — contributing crucial runs and wickets — helped Australia beat India by five runs to enter their seventh consecutive final.

 

• Australia went on to win the tournament, defeating South Africa in the final, also held at Newlands, Cape Town.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2023 Women's T20 World Cup was hosted by South Africa, the first time the tournament was held on African soil.

 

NOTE

 

• Deepti Sharma (Option 1): An Indian all-rounder who played in this semi-final for India, but was not adjudged Player of the Match.

 

• Meg Lanning (Option 3): Captained Australia in this tournament but was not the Player of the Match in this particular semi-final.

 

• Harmanpreet Kaur (Option 4): Captained the Indian team in this semi-final but did not receive the Player of the Match award.

question: As per article 123, the ordinance making power is the most important legislative power of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 123 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to promulgate ordinances when either House of Parliament (or both) is not in session, provided he/she is satisfied that circumstances require immediate action. (अनुच्छेद 123 — अध्यादेश जारी करने की शक्ति, राष्ट्रपति)

 

• An ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, but it must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and approved within six weeks of reassembly, failing which it ceases to operate.

 

• This ordinance-making power is regarded as the most important legislative power of the President, allowing the executive to respond quickly to urgent situations when Parliament is not in session.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A parallel provision, Article 213, grants similar ordinance-making power to State Governors.

 

• An ordinance can be withdrawn by the President at any time and cannot be used to amend the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajya Sabha (Option 2): As one of the two Houses of Parliament, it has legislative powers, but it does not possess ordinance-making power.

 

• Legislative council (Option 3): An upper house at the state level; it has no ordinance-making power.

 

• Chief Justice of India (Option 4): Heads the judiciary and has no legislative or ordinance-making power.

question: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1931.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin. (गांधी-इरविन समझौता — 1931)

 

• Under the pact, the Civil Disobedience Movement was suspended, and the government agreed to release political prisoners who had not committed acts of violence.

 

• It also enabled Gandhi's participation, as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress, in the Second Round Table Conference held in London later in 1931.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The pact is also known as the Delhi Pact.

 

• The Civil Disobedience Movement had been launched by Gandhi in 1930 with the Dandi Salt March.

 

NOTE

 

• 1935 (Option 1): This is the year the Government of India Act, 1935 was passed, unrelated to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

 

• 1929 (Option 2): This is the year of the Lahore session of the Congress, where the resolution for Purna Swaraj (complete independence) was adopted.

 

• 1941 (Option 4): Not connected to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

question: Which of the following schemes was launched for the welfare of the unorganised sector workers and labourers on 26 August 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is e-Shram Portal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The e-Shram Portal was launched on 26 August 2021 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to create a comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW), covering workers such as migrant labourers, gig and platform workers, construction workers, etc. (ई-श्रम पोर्टल — 26 अगस्त 2021)

 

• Workers registering on the portal receive a 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) and become eligible for benefits under various social security schemes.

 

• The portal also provides accident insurance cover under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) to registered workers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The e-Shram database aims to help the government design and target welfare schemes more effectively for the estimated 40+ crore unorganised sector workers in India.

 

NOTE

 

• PM Mentoring Yuva Scheme (Option 2): A scheme aimed at fostering mentorship, entrepreneurship and skill-building among youth, not launched on 26 August 2021 for unorganised workers.

 

• PM Daksh Yojana (Option 3): A skill development scheme for marginalised groups run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, distinct from e-Shram, which is specifically the unorganised-worker database launched on 26 August 2021.

 

• Gram Ujala Scheme (Option 4): A rural LED bulb distribution scheme, unrelated to unorganised sector worker welfare.

question: What is the SI unit of current?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ampere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A), named after French physicist André-Marie Ampère. (विद्युत धारा की SI इकाई — एम्पियर)

 

• One ampere is defined based on the elementary charge, fixed as exactly 1.602176634×10⁻¹⁹ coulombs, under the current SI definition (revised in 2019).

 

• Electric current is one of the seven base quantities in the SI system, alongside length, mass, time, temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related electrical quantities include: Ohm (Ω) for resistance, Volt (V) for potential difference, and Watt (W) for power.

 

NOTE

 

• Ohm (Option 1): This is the SI unit of electrical resistance, not current.

 

• Metre (Option 3): This is the SI unit of length, not current.

 

• Volt (Option 4): This is the SI unit of electric potential/voltage, not current.

question: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hyponatremia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hyponatremia is an electrolyte disorder in which the concentration of sodium in the blood becomes abnormally low (below 135 mmol/L), which can cause cells to swell and lead to symptoms like nausea, headache, confusion and, in severe cases, seizures. (हाइपोनेट्रीमिया — रक्त में सोडियम की कमी)

 

• It can result from excessive fluid intake, certain medications, kidney or heart disease, or hormonal imbalances (e.g., SIADH).

 

• Treatment typically involves correcting the underlying cause and, in some cases, carefully restricting fluids or administering sodium under medical supervision.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sodium (Na⁺) is the primary electrolyte regulating fluid balance and blood pressure in the body; its normal blood range is about 135-145 mmol/L.

 

NOTE

 

• Hyperkalemia (Option 1): Refers to abnormally high potassium levels in the blood, not low sodium.

 

• Hypokalemia (Option 2): Refers to abnormally low potassium levels in the blood, not sodium.

 

• Hypernatremia (Option 4): Refers to abnormally high sodium levels in the blood — the opposite of what the question describes.

question: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described Directive Principles of State Policy as __________of the Indian constitution.
option_3: The mostprecious part of the constitution
option_4: a novel feature of the constitution
solution_text:
The correct answer is a novel feature of the constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, in the Constituent Assembly debates, described the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) as a "novel feature" of the Indian Constitution, since no other constitution combined justiciable Fundamental Rights with non-justiciable socio-economic guiding principles in this manner. (नीति निदेशक तत्व — संविधान की 'नवीन विशेषता')

 

• The DPSPs, contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution, are non-justiciable guidelines directing the State to establish social and economic democracy, drawing inspiration from the Irish Constitution.

 

• While DPSPs are not enforceable by courts, Article 37 states they are nevertheless "fundamental in the governance of the country" and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Legal scholar Granville Austin described the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles together as the "Conscience of the Constitution."

 

NOTE

 

• Soul of the state (Option 1): Not the phrase used by Ambedkar for DPSP; a distractor option.

 

• Identity card of the constitution (Option 2): Not Ambedkar's description of the DPSPs; a distractor option.

 

• The mostprecious part of the constitution (Option 3): Not the phrase Ambedkar used for DPSPs; a distractor option.

question: Tera Tali folk dance is primarily associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tera Tali is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, performed predominantly by women of the Kamada (Kamad) community, seated on the ground and tying manjeeras (cymbals) to their bodies at 13 points. (तेरह ताली नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• The dance is performed as a devotional offering to Baba Ramdev (Ramdevji), a revered folk deity of Rajasthan, and dancers often balance swords or pots on their heads while performing.

 

• "Tera Tali" literally means "thirteen claps/cymbals", referring to the number of manjeeras tied to the performer's body.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Kalbelia and Chari.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Bihu, not Tera Tali.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Known for dances like Karma and Gaur Maria, not Tera Tali.

 

• Haryana (Option 4): Known for dances like Ghoomar (regional variant) and Dhamal, not Tera Tali.

question: Who among the following was the Vakil under the reign of Mughal Emperor, Akbar, who received the title of Khan-i-Khanan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bairam Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bairam Khan served as the Vakil (regent/chief minister) during the early years of Emperor Akbar's reign (1556-1560) and was honoured with the title "Khan-i-Khanan" ("Khan of Khans"). (बैरम खान — खान-ए-खाना)

 

• Bairam Khan had earlier played a decisive role in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), which secured the Mughal throne for the young Akbar after Humayun's death.

 

• He effectively administered the empire as regent until 1560, after which Akbar assumed direct control and Bairam Khan's regency ended.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• After his dismissal, Bairam Khan was assassinated in 1561 at Patan, Gujarat, while on his way for Hajj pilgrimage.

 

NOTE

 

• Mulla do-Piyaza (Option 1): A courtier figure remembered in folklore alongside Birbal, not the Vakil who held the title Khan-i-Khanan.

 

• Birbal (Option 2): One of Akbar's Navratnas (Nine Gems), renowned for wit and wisdom, not the Vakil/regent.

 

• Raja Todar Mal (Option 3): Another of Akbar's Navratnas, famous for his revenue (land) reforms, not the Vakil holding the title Khan-i-Khanan.
